title: hook-priority-scheduler-and-template-dependency-resolution
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce a hook priority scheduler and deterministic template dependency resolution for the private installer Helm charts and hook jobs. Motivation: tenants with large numbers of tenant-scoped init hooks were occasionally triggering concurrent heavy migrations and image pulls that caused network/registry rate limits and prolonged upgrade windows. This PR adds (1) a scheduler that assigns hook execution windows and priority buckets to init hooks via values.yaml configuration, (2) deterministic template dependency graph resolution so hooks declared with 'requires' ordering are applied consistently across helm renders and upgrades, and (3) an optional init-rate-limiter sidecar controller integration that coordinates cross-tenant concurrency using a ConfigMap-backed lease. The change includes: - new values schema fields (hookGroups, priorityBuckets, templateDeps, rateLimiter) with validation in values.schema.json - Helm template helpers for rendering hook annotations, leader-elector labels and per-tenant retries - A CRD-compatible annotation convention so the private-installer can surface hook group statuses to the installer controller (note: does not introduce a new CRD in this PR; uses annotated ConfigMaps for compatibility) - Unit and integration tests for template rendering and scheduler policy - Migration notes to preserve previous installs and a small upgrade hook to mark existing non-annotated hook resources for controller adoption Backwards compatibility: defaults keep existing behavior (all hooks single group, FIFO within group). Operators that opt in get controlled ramping and deterministic ordering. See linked Linear tasks and in-PR checklist for rollout steps.
commit_summary: scheduler: add hook-priority-scheduler library and policy config
helm: extend _helpers.tpl with renderHookMeta and resolveTemplateDeps functions
values.schema.json: add hookGroups, priorityBuckets, templateDeps and rateLimiter entries with validation
tests: add templating unit tests and an integration smoke harness for init-rate-limiter interactions
review_comments: Mateo: Can you make priorityBuckets optional when hookGroups is not set? Asha: yes, default is constructed in helpers.tpl when absent. Sophie: I noticed a race between the annotate-existing-resources upgrade hook and controller adoption in the first run; added a conditional backoff and a two-phase annotate step. Jordan: please add a note to the upgrade playbook about rate-limiter ConfigMap RBAC requirements. Once tests green I'll approve. After two CI reruns and a small mock time fix in policy_test.go approvals were provided and the PR was merged via squash.
release_notes: Add hook priority scheduling and deterministic template dependency resolution for private-installer Helm charts; introduce optional init rate limiter integration to coordinate hook concurrency across tenants. Backwards compatible by default; operators must opt-in via values.yaml. See docs/helm/hook-groups.md for configuration examples and the upgrade playbook for migration steps.
test_plan: Unit: policy_test.go covers priority buckets and dependency resolution permutations. Helm template tests validate rendered annotations and labels. Integration: init-rate-limiter-smoke runs a mini-cluster smoke test that simulates parallel tenant upgrades and asserts max concurrent hook jobs. Manual: follow upgrade playbook in docs/helm/upgrade-playbook.md to roll out on staging and verify annotate-existing-resources hook completes before controller adoption.
notes: This PR intentionally avoids introducing a CRD to reduce upgrade friction. If future work requires richer state, we'll propose a CRD migration path. Operators with strict air-gapped installs should pin the rate-limiter image and enable the sidecar controller via values to avoid external dependencies. The change was demoed during the infra sync on 2026-02-12.
